purpose: Olanzapine is used to treat conditions like schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. It helps reduce symptoms such as hallucinations, delusions, and severe mood swings. It can also be used short-term to treat agitation related to these conditions.
how_it_works: Your brain uses chemical messengers called dopamine and serotonin to communicate between nerve cells. In conditions like schizophrenia or bipolar disorder, these chemicals can become unbalanced. Olanzapine works by blocking certain receptors for these chemicals, helping to restore balance and reduce symptoms like confused thinking and extreme mood changes.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or feeling sleepy, weight gain, increased appetite, dry mouth, dizziness when standing up, constipation, and feeling restless or having trouble sitting still. Some people may also notice higher blood sugar or cholesterol levels over time.
warnings: This medication can cause significant weight gain and raise your blood sugar, so regular check-ups are important. It should not be used in elderly patients with dementia-related behavior problems as it can increase the risk of stroke or death. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as symptoms may return. Tell your doctor if you have diabetes, liver problems, or a history of seizures.
typical_dosing: For most adults, the starting dose is usually 5 to 10 mg taken once a day, typically at bedtime because it can cause drowsiness. Your doctor may slowly increase the dose over time based on how you respond, up to a maximum of 20 mg per day. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes, and try to take it at the same time each day.
